title: Value betting
description: Six questions on the by-worse criterion, sizing tiers, and geometric three-street planning.

questions.prompt: Which definition of a value bet matches the curriculum?

choices.text: Any bet made on the river.
A bet that wins the pot at least 50% of the time when called.
A bet where you expect more *worse* hands than *better* hands to call.
A bet sized to fold out all weaker hands.

questions.explanation: The by-worse criterion: bet for value when the calling range contains more worse hands than better hands. If only better hands call, you're value-owning yourself.

questions.prompt: Which sizing tier is appropriate for a thin value bet (e.g. weak top pair on a coordinated turn)?
questions.explanation: Thin value uses 25–40% to keep wide weak ranges in and minimise loss to raises from better. Larger sizings fold the entire range you wanted to charge.

questions.prompt: 100bb effective in a 3-bet pot at SPR ≈ 5. What is the per-street bet (as a fraction of pot, 2 decimals) needed to get all-in over three streets?
An overbet on the river (1.5×–2× pot) is correct when you hold a TPTK in a single-raised pot, because TPTK is a clear value hand.
questions.explanation: Overbets target villain's bluff-catcher range and require *nut advantage*. TPTK is one pair — it gets raised by better and folds out worse. Use a standard value sizing instead.

questions.prompt: Why is a three-street geometric stack-off rarely the right plan in a single-raised pot at 100bb?

choices.text: SPR ≈ 17, so geometric sizing requires ~115% pot per street — overbets villain's range will not pay.
SRPs always go to showdown with no betting.
100bb is too shallow for geometric play.

questions.explanation: At SPR ≈ 17 the geometric size is ~1.13× pot, which is an overbet on every street. Villain's range simply won't pay this — you have to abandon the stack-off plan or use the river jam as the overbet.

questions.prompt: Which questions should you ask before choosing a value bet size? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Which calling range am I targeting?
How does this size compare to my bluff frequency?
How committed am I given the SPR?
Is the wind direction favouring small bets today?

questions.explanation: Calling range, bluff/value balance, and commitment via SPR all matter. Wind direction does not.
